newsitem.title: FRANCE: CADES sells Ffr bond, plans Japanese domestic bond.
newsitem.headline: CADES sells Ffr bond, plans Japanese domestic bond.

text.p: French welfare debt repayment fund CADES said on Wednesday it had sold a 650 million franc domestic bond to a limited number of investors in an operation lead managed by JP Morgan.
It said in a statement the issue had a maturity of 11 years although CADES had an option to repay the bond at the end of the sixth year.
CADES also said it was planning to issue a bond on the Japanese domestic market towards the end of April to be lead managed by Daiwa Securities and Nikko Securities, market conditions permitting.
A CADES spokesman said the size of the issue had not been finalised but he said the issue would probably be a dual currency bond, issued in yen and repaid in another currency.
As expected, CADES said it had decided to reduce its syndicated loan facility to 26.6 billion francs from 60 billion francs currently.
CADES chairman Benoit Jolivet said in March it planned to reduce the loan facility, which it was not currently using, to around 30 billion francs to save costs.
Jolivet said in March the fund was planning private placements and was also looking at the yen market although a decision to issue in yen would depend on swap rates being favourable.
It said details of the yen issue would be available in the coming days.

CADES (Caisse d'Amortissement de la Dette Sociale) was launched in April 1996 to repay 140 billion francs of accumulated social security debt by January 2009, taking the burden off the welfare system.
